notice: HELD-OUT confirmation set for the POST-HOC Article 5(1)(c) intervention (SYSTEM_SPEC.md §18, opened 2026-10-04). Built and committed BEFORE any change to the matcher prompt or logic, and not run or inspected against any model output during iteration. It is used for ONE confirmation pass only, after user approval, and its results are reported separately from the 41-case dev set. The angles deliberately differ from the 12 dev cases where 5(1)(c) came back insufficient: payment fraud, workplace productivity scoring, churn risk, motor telematics pricing, buy-now-pay-later credit, an employer scoring private social-media behaviour (positive control), and two cases where the information that decides 5(1)(c) is missing (borderline, gold unresolved). Labels follow the dev set's labelling_rules unchanged.

cases.description: Our payment company built a model that gives every card transaction a fraud-risk score in real time. Transactions with a high score are held until a fraud analyst has reviewed them.

gold_facts.ai_functionality: scores card transactions for fraud risk
gold_facts.role_in_decision_making: high-score transactions held for analyst review

cases.labelling_note: Fraud detection scores transactions, not people's social behaviour; Annex III 5(b) expressly excludes financial-fraud detection.

cases.description: We bought PickRate, which scores each warehouse worker's productivity from their handheld-scanner data. Shift managers use the weekly scores to allocate tasks and to decide who is offered extra shifts.

gold_facts.ai_functionality: scores worker productivity from scanner data
gold_facts.role_in_decision_making: managers use scores to allocate tasks and extra shifts

cases.labelling_note: Performance evaluation used within the same work context is Annex III 4(b), not a social score applied in unrelated contexts.

cases.description: Our telecom company built a model that predicts which customers are likely to cancel their contract, from their usage and billing history. Customers flagged as likely to leave are offered a discount.

gold_facts.ai_functionality: predicts customer churn from usage and billing history
gold_facts.role_in_decision_making: flagged customers are offered a discount

cases.labelling_note: Generic risk score of people whose stated consequence is favourable treatment (a discount) in the same context: no detrimental treatment.

cases.description: We are a car insurer and developed an app that customers can choose to install. It scores their driving each month (speed, harsh braking, night driving), and the score moves their motor-insurance premium up or down.
cases.labelling_note: Driving data used to price motor insurance: same context, and the consequence tracks the behaviour scored. Annex III 5(c) covers life and health insurance only.

cases.description: We built and run a buy-now-pay-later service. At checkout it decides how much credit each shopper can get, based on their repayment history with us and a credit-bureau check.

gold_facts.ai_functionality: sets each shopper's credit limit from repayment history and a credit-bureau check

cases.labelling_note: Creditworthiness assessment (Annex III 5(b)) using financial data in the credit context; not social scoring.

cases.description: As an employer, we use a tool that monitors our employees' personal social-media accounts and rates their behaviour outside work over the year. Employees with low ratings are excluded from bonuses and promotions.

gold_facts.role_in_decision_making: low ratings exclude employees from bonuses and promotions

cases.labelling_note: Positive control: social behaviour in private life, scored over time, leading to detrimental treatment at work (an unrelated context, 5(1)(c)(i)). Risk tier is separate (DL3): promotion decisions are Annex III 4(b).

cases.description: We built our supermarket's loyalty app. It gives each member a behaviour rating based on how they shop and act in our stores, and members with a low rating are treated differently.

gold_facts.role_in_decision_making: members with low ratings are treated differently

cases.labelling_note: Borderline: people are scored on behaviour, but whether the different treatment is detrimental, and whether it is disproportionate or in an unrelated context, is not stated. Tests that the fix does not turn genuine silence into does_not_match.

cases.description: Our city council developed a system that scores residents on their civic behaviour over the year, such as recycling and noise complaints. We have not yet decided what the scores will be used for.
cases.labelling_note: Borderline: social behaviour scored over time, but the consequence (the part 5(1)(c) turns on) and the use (Annex III) are undecided. Same convention as dev D31.
